title: Describe the capabilities and function of TFTP/FTP in the network

questions.question: Which command restore configuration to the running-config for a device from a server?

correct.explanation: copy tftp: running-config restores a saved config from TFTP directly into running-config.

incorrect.explanation: archive tftp: manages configuration archives — standard restore uses copy tftp: running-config.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch#archive tftp: running-config points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for configuration.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "configuration", Switch#copy tftp: running-config satisfies what this question tests — Switch#archive tftp: running-config does not.

incorrect.explanation: restore tftp://... is not valid IOS — use interactive copy tftp: running-config.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch#restore tftp://192.168.1.2 running-config names an automation tool, data format, or API style that may not match the stem's orchestration model.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "configuration", Switch#copy tftp: running-config satisfies what this question tests — Switch#restore tftp://192.168.1.2 running-config does not.

incorrect.explanation: copy server: is not the TFTP syntax — source is tftp: (or ftp:, scp:).
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch#copy server: running-config points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for configuration.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "configuration", Switch#copy tftp: running-config satisfies what this question tests — Switch#copy server: running-config does not.

answerReview.examTip: Config restore: copy tftp: running-config (immediate) | copy tftp: startup-config (+ reload for boot).

questions.question: Which command begin the upgrade of an IOS from a TFTP server?

correct.explanation: copy tftp flash (privileged EXEC) downloads the IOS image from TFTP into flash — the standard upgrade starting command.

incorrect.explanation: copy tftp ios is invalid — the destination keyword is flash, not ios.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Invented ios destination for TFTP copy
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch#copy tftp ios points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for tftp.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "tftp", Switch#copy tftp flash satisfies what this question tests — Switch#copy tftp ios does not.

incorrect.explanation: copy tftp nvram targets startup-config storage — IOS images go to flash.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch#copy tftp nvram points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for tftp.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "tftp", Switch#copy tftp flash satisfies what this question tests — Switch#copy tftp nvram does not.

incorrect.explanation: upgrade tftp flash is not valid IOS syntax — use copy tftp flash.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch#upgrade tftp flash points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for tftp.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "tftp", Switch#copy tftp flash satisfies what this question tests — Switch#upgrade tftp flash does not.

answerReview.examTip: IOS upgrade: copy tftp flash → verify with show flash: → set boot system → reload.

questions.question: Which command can boot a router from a TFTP server for the image of c2900-universalk9-mz.SPA.151-4.M4.bin on the TFTP server of 192.168.1.2?
questions.explanation: boot system tftp://192.168.1.2 c2900-universalk9-mz.SPA.151-4.M4.bin — Cisco-style TFTP URL then image filename in global config.

correct.explanation: boot system tftp://192.168.1.2 c2900-universalk9-mz.SPA.151-4.M4.bin — Cisco-style TFTP URL then image filename in global config.

incorrect.explanation: boot tftp:// is privileged EXEC syntax — boot system belongs in global config and needs the image filename.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Attempts a privileged-EXEC boot with only a TFTP URL.

incorrect.explanation: Missing system keyword — IOS uses boot system tftp://<server> <filename>.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Uses boot without the system keyword.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Correct form is boot system tftp://192.168.1.2 <image.bin>.

incorrect.explanation: Filename before the TFTP URL reverses the usual Cisco boot system tftp://… <filename> order.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Places the image name before the tftp:// URL.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Keyed syntax is boot system tftp://192.168.1.2 c2900-universalk9-mz.SPA.151-4.M4.bin.

answerReview.examTip: Boot from TFTP: boot system tftp://<ip> <image.bin> in global config + copy tftp flash first.

questions.question: You’re upgrading the flash memory on a 2900 router with a brand-new flash card. What needs to be done to restore the IOS?
choices: The new flash memory will have a mini-IOS installed. You will need to upgrade it from the mini-IOS.
The router will boot into the ROMMON, and from there you will need to TFTP download the IOS.
Nothing needs to be done because the IOS is not storage on the flash memory card.
Format the flash card with the FAT operating system and copy the IOS image to the card.

correct.explanation: A blank flash card leaves no valid IOS — the router boots to ROMMON and you TFTP-download the image.

incorrect.explanation: New flash is empty, not pre-loaded with mini-IOS — you must recover via ROMMON/TFTP.
incorrect.whatItDoes: The new flash memory will have a mini-IOS installed. You will need to upgrade it from the mini-IOS. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for upgrading.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "upgrading", The router will boot into the ROMMON, and from there you will need to TFTP download the IOS. satisfies what this question tests — The new flash memory will have a mini-IOS installed. You will need to upgrade it from the mini-IOS. does not.

incorrect.explanation: IOS is stored on flash — without an image the device cannot boot normally.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Nothing needs to be done because the IOS is not storage on the flash memory card. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for upgrading.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "upgrading", The router will boot into the ROMMON, and from there you will need to TFTP download the IOS. satisfies what this question tests — Nothing needs to be done because the IOS is not storage on the flash memory card. does not.

incorrect.explanation: Formatting alone does not place an IOS image — you still need to copy the image to flash.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Format the flash card with the FAT operating system and copy the IOS image to the card. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for upgrading.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "upgrading", The router will boot into the ROMMON, and from there you will need to TFTP download the IOS. satisfies what this question tests — Format the flash card with the FAT operating system and copy the IOS image to the card. does not.

answerReview.examTip: Dead flash / blank card → ROMMON → set IP/TFTP vars → tftpdnld or copy tftp flash.

questions.question: Which command(s) are required before you can use an FTP server for backing up configuration? Assume that the username is USER and the password is USERPASS.
choices: Router(config)#ip ftp username USER password USERPASS
Router(config)#ip ftp username USER Router(config)#ip ftp password USERPASS

correct.explanation: FTP credentials use two global commands: ip ftp username USER and ip ftp password USERPASS.

incorrect.explanation: password cannot appear on the same line as ip ftp username — split into two commands.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config)#ip ftp username USER password USERPASS points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for required.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "required", Router(config)#ip ftp username USER Router(config)#ip ftp password USERPASS satisfies what this question tests — Router(config)#ip ftp username USER password USERPASS does not.

incorrect.explanation: ftp USER password is not valid IOS global syntax.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config)#ftp USER password USERPASS points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for required.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "required", Router(config)#ip ftp username USER Router(config)#ip ftp password USERPASS satisfies what this question tests — Router(config)#ftp USER password USERPASS does not.

incorrect.explanation: username creates local login accounts — FTP copy uses ip ftp username/password.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Router(config)#username USER password USERPASS points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for required.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "required", Router(config)#ip ftp username USER Router(config)#ip ftp password USERPASS satisfies what this question tests — Router(config)#username USER password USERPASS does not.

answerReview.examTip: FTP backup: ip ftp username + ip ftp password → copy running-config ftp:.
